evidence: ecc/skills/skill-comply/SKILL.md:12-16 varies prompts from supportive to neutral to competing and checks behavioral ordering. eval/README.md:30 describes assertions over prose, artifacts and gates; eval/run.mjs:198-234 extracts text and subagent presence rather than general action sequences.
problem: An additional regression dimension is available: whether an instruction survives a prompt that omits its reminders or encourages a conflicting shortcut. Successful explicitly guided cases do not establish that independence.
proposal: Extend the existing manual eval harness with hand-authored neutral and competing prompt variants for a few high-value rules, using existing artifact/gate assertions first. Keep expectations human-authored rather than importing automatic LLM grading. Add test/eval-prompt-variants.test.mjs for variant selection and result attribution. Maintenance: a small fixed scenario set, with model runs remaining manual; complements the already accepted authority-suite finding.

evidence: superpowers/skills/receiving-code-review/SKILL.md:67-83 checks reviewer suggestions against actual behavior, compatibility and prior decisions before implementing. rules/agent/autonomy.md:13-14 says to fix CRITICAL findings; its authority section at line 53 establishes that review opinions are proposals but supplies no corresponding verification step.
problem: The field offers a useful operational bridge between mandatory review remediation and the local principle that reviewers propose rather than decide: verify a reported defect before changing working behavior.
proposal: Add a compact clause beside the existing review-remediation step: confirm the finding against code, requirements and supported versions; fix confirmed defects, and escalate an unsupported blocking finding with evidence. Preserve review-report ownership and hard-bypass rules. Maintenance: one authoritative clause, without a new skill or the source's conversational prohibitions.

evidence: ecc/skills/benchmark-optimization-loop/SKILL.md:15-37 requires a measured baseline, correctness gate, identical input shape and confirmation reruns; lines 54-58 compare against the accepted winner and stop within measurement noise. skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:99-110 records objective, done-command and caps without an optimization-specific comparison protocol.
problem: A bounded optimization loop benefits from more than a green done-command: comparable measurements and preserved correctness prevent promoting a faster variant that changed the workload or weakened the result.
proposal: Add an on-demand optimization reference to loop-setup: fixed workload/environment, baseline command and result, separate correctness command, one hypothesis per variant, repeated baseline/winner measurements, and a noise-based stopping rule. Feature changes retain the RFC path. Maintenance: one short reference and one focused eval fixture; no generic benchmark framework or hardware-dependent CI threshold.

evidence: superpowers/skills/diagnosing-superpowers/SKILL.md:15-17 requires transcript citations and measured numbers; lines 23-43 scope the complaint, verify session identity and inspect recorded events. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:7-15 reconstructs the implementation from the current conversation; lines 19-20 deliberately keep it inline and user-invoked.
problem: The existing retrospective does not provide a procedure for investigating a past failed agent session, such as repeated work or ignored instructions, using recorded events rather than the agent's recollection.
proposal: Extend debrief with an explicitly requested session-diagnosis branch and an on-demand reference: identify the transcript and relevant turn range, separate human prompts from tool/hook output, cite observed failures, and distinguish observed facts from inferred causes. Keep the default inline and read-only; do not import seven mandatory analysts, automatic exports or automatic rule edits. Maintenance: documented transcript adapters for supported hosts, with unsupported formats reported explicitly.

evidence: The guide says Claude never loads AGENTS.md as a fallback. Current official documentation says Claude Code v2.1.277+ can load it when project CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md files are absent, subject to configuration and availability: [Claude Code memory documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#agents-md). mattpocock-skills/skills/productivity/writing-for-agents/SKILL.md:79 identifies environment documentation restatements as caches that can become stale.
problem: The vendor convention has changed, so the guide now incorrectly tells AGENTS.md-only repositories that Claude starts without project instructions.
proposal: Correct the existing guide with the version floor, default fallback condition and documented exceptions. Retain the current per-agent emission architecture; changing that would require separate architectural exploration. Maintenance: date and link this vendor-specific statement so future audits can recheck its source.
